viral_brainrot.name: Viral Brainrot
comedy_types: overconfident character facing a simple problem
character trying to accomplish something ridiculous
character protecting something unimportant as if it were extremely valuable
character attempting something clearly beyond its ability
character competing against an unexpected opponent
character reacting dramatically to an ordinary problem
character caught in an unexpectedly embarrassing situation
tiny character dealing with something enormous
large character struggling with something tiny
rules: The protagonist must be a living being or character-like creature.
The protagonist must have a visible face and readable emotional reaction.
Inanimate objects may appear only as props, obstacles, environments, or consequences.
Never make an inanimate object the protagonist or primary acting entity.
Every clip must work completely independently.
Do not create continuity between clips.
Do not require the same character to appear in multiple clips.
Do not require dialogue.
Do not require narration.
The visual joke must be understandable without sound.
The premise must be simple enough to understand immediately.
The character should have a clear goal, intention, or desire.
The character should encounter one simple problem or obstacle.
The character should visibly react to the problem.
Use one primary comedic idea per clip.
Use one natural escalation rather than many unrelated events.
End with a clear visual payoff.
Avoid random destruction without a comedic reason.
Avoid meaningless chaos.
Avoid long setups.
Avoid static characters simply watching events happen.
Avoid long chains of unrelated actions.
Prioritize character behavior and facial reactions over spectacle.
Prioritize curiosity and visual clarity over complexity.

generation.camera_style: clear cinematic movement that follows the character and supports the joke

requirements: Generate independent concepts rather than a connected story.
Give each concept one clear comedic premise.
Choose a protagonist from the configured protagonist types.
Make the protagonist visually expressive and emotionally readable.
Make the premise understandable from the first visual moment.
Create immediate curiosity without a slow introduction.
Give the protagonist a simple visible goal or intention.
Introduce one clear obstacle or problem.
Use character behavior and reaction as the main source of comedy.
Use physical movement and environmental interaction when appropriate.
End with a satisfying visual payoff.
Keep the action simple enough for text-to-video generation.
Use variety across the requested clips.
Do not repeat the same type of protagonist, premise, or comedic mechanism unnecessarily.
Do not make objects the protagonist.
Do not create traditional multi-scene stories.
Do not require dialogue, narration, or text on screen.
End every prompt with the configured visual style.
